title: BORN IN A STABLE
text: She gave birth to her firstborn son. She wrapped him in bands of cloth and laid him in a feeding trough, because there was no room for them in the inn.

body.kids: Jesus was born where the animals were kept. His first bed was the box the animals ate from. God did not arrive at the top — he arrived at the bottom.
body.teens: Luke dates the birth by imperial decree, then puts the Son of God in a feeding trough. The contrast is the argument: the announcement goes to shepherds, not to the palace.

q.kids: Where was Jesus laid after he was born?
q.teens: Where does Luke say Jesus was laid?

why.kids: A manger — the box animals eat from.
why.teens: A manger. Luke's whole gospel keeps this downward shape.

title: TWELVE ORDINARY MEN
text: Jesus said to them, “Come after me, and I will make you into fishers for men.”

body.kids: Jesus picked fishermen, a tax collector, and ordinary people — not the ones everyone expected.
body.teens: He chose twelve, deliberately echoing the twelve tribes. The claim underneath the choice is about the renewal of Israel, not just about staffing.

q.kids: What job did some of the first disciples have?
q.teens: What was the trade of the first disciples Jesus called?

why.kids: They caught fish for a living.
why.teens: Fishermen from around Galilee — working men, not scholars.

title: HE CALMED THE STORM
text: He awoke and rebuked the wind, and said to the sea, “Peace! Be still!” The wind ceased and there was a great calm.

body.kids: The disciples were terrified. Jesus was asleep. He stood up, told the storm to stop — and it stopped.
body.teens: Mark ends the scene on a question, not a rescue: who is this? Authority over the sea belongs to God alone in the Hebrew Bible, and Mark's readers would have heard it.

q.kids: What did Jesus say to the storm?
q.teens: How does Mark end the storm episode?

why.kids: He spoke to the storm like a person, and it obeyed.
why.teens: With the disciples more frightened after the calm than during the storm.

title: THE CROSS
text: Jesus said, “Father, forgive them, for they don’t know what they are doing.”

body.kids: Jesus had done nothing wrong. He was killed anyway — and while it happened, he asked God to forgive the people doing it.
body.teens: Crucifixion was designed to be public and humiliating. Luke records Pilate finding no guilt three times. The forgiveness is spoken from inside the execution, not afterwards.

q.kids: What did Jesus say about the people who hurt him?
q.teens: What does Luke record Jesus saying from the cross?

why.kids: He asked his Father to forgive them.
why.teens: A prayer for his executioners — Luke's distinctive record of the crucifixion.

title: THE EMPTY TOMB
text: “Why do you seek the living among the dead? He isn’t here, but is risen!”

body.kids: On Sunday morning the stone was rolled away and the tomb was empty. Jesus was alive, and he ate breakfast with his friends.
body.teens: The first witnesses are women, whose testimony carried little legal weight — an unlikely detail to invent. Paul's summary in 1 Corinthians 15 lists named witnesses and says most were still alive to ask.

q.kids: What did the women find at the tomb?
q.teens: Who are the first witnesses to the empty tomb?

why.teens: Women, which is precisely what makes the detail hard to explain as invention.
